scope: Exact XML 1.0 Fifth Edition NCName/QName validation for inert ACCDT control XML, schema metadata and table data
acceptance: Explicit XML NameStartChar/NameChar scalar ranges with colon excluded for NCName; no Unicode category approximation, normalization or case folding.

Independent start-range endpoints and exclusions, continuation-only middle dot/combining/connector characters, superscript-category counterexamples, supplementary name starts and U+EFFFF/U+F0000 boundary.
Raw schema declaration NCNames validated before single-pass Access _xHHHH_ decoding; escaped spaces/colons remain stored field names.
Trimmed XSD type/base/ref QNames validated before namespace resolution; malformed components and undeclared prefixes fail without external schema access.
Element and attribute QNames, including namespace declarations, checked in bounded tree and flat control readers; namespace identity remains URI based.
Original package tests across UTF-8, BOM UTF-8 and both BOM UTF-16 byte orders preserve exact field names, scalar rows and original bytes.
Existing CJK names remain supported; exact Unicode prefixes resolve unchanged, including supplementary and combining continuations.
Metadata discovery still stops after the complete schema before malformed source units or data events; cumulative work and cancellation remain authoritative.
counting_notes: All seven new tests plus 59 existing template tests passed on the first focused run. Strict Access lib/tests passed without lint or golden corrections.
After tests and strict checks, one blank line was added between existing schema helper functions; no behavior changed. Scoped formatter and diff checks passed.
Strict lib/tests checks compile and lint test targets; no additional full suite is claimed.
limitations: Original authored XML/ZIP tests and primary XML grammar establish engineering behavior, not native Access template instantiation or full XSD/XML implementation qualification.
Existing encoding, package, XML byte, node, attribute and schema limits remain unchanged. DTDs, general entity expansion, external schemas/providers and unsupported XSD shapes remain refused.
SQL/native database names and OPC part-name rules are separate and unchanged. Schema prefix validation does not validate an unread record suffix.
